primitives.verbatim_quote: Auth — the `/api/user` proxy + login/logout Every app is authenticated.
primitives.assumptions: User identity is established via secure token exchange with backend.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs on invalid or expired session tokens.

layer2.mapping: GSI tracks session validity through token lifecycle; GSE enforces access control via middleware.

primitives.name: SDK Client Instantiation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Create the SDK clients (server-side) One adapter satisfies jobs + media + profile.
primitives.assumptions: Server-side instantiation ensures consistent adapter behavior across services.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs on misconfigured or missing adapter factories.

layer2.mapping: GSE constructs service-specific clients from shared workflow platform adapter; GSI validates client configuration against schema.
layer2.telemetry: Client creation latency, adapter registration count

primitives.name: Job Submission With Confirmation Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Submit (with the confirmation gate) → poll → read the URL The `confirm` gate is passed to the **adapter factory**; it runs once per submit, after validation, before any network call.
primitives.assumptions: Confirmation gate acts as a preflight validator ensuring semantic correctness.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Rejection due to user cancellation or validation error.

layer2.mapping: GSI models confirmation logic as probabilistic decision tree; GSE enforces gate execution before network I/O.
layer2.telemetry: Submission success rate, confirmation rejection frequency

The critical path embodies a structured sequence: authentication establishes trust, SDK instantiation provides abstraction layers, job submission triggers computation with safety checks, and polling enables asynchronous result retrieval. Each stage must maintain integrity through defined interfaces. Auth pipelines ensure secure identity management; SDK clients abstract service interactions into reusable modules. Job submission includes a confirmation gate that prevents erroneous operations. Polling allows for non-blocking interaction with backend systems. Rendering consumes final outputs while respecting UI constraints such as aspect ratios and preview availability. These primitives form a closed-loop system where errors propagate predictably through well-defined boundaries. Failure modes include token expiration, misconfigured adapters, and rejected submissions. The design enforces immutability of data flows and restricts side effects to controlled entry points.
